capture.final_message:
Treat the two conjuncts independently.

- For the first, use the meromorphic argument principle on the rectangle. The logarithmic derivative \(f'/f\) has residue \(\operatorname{ord}_p(f)\) at each zero or pole \(p\). The boundary-disjointness assumption permits the residue theorem, while finite order and local finiteness make the divisor support inside the compact rectangle finite. Thus the rectangle integral equals the finite sum of the divisor multiplicities.

- Near \(s=1\), remove the simple pole of \(\zeta\) by setting
  \[
  g(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s).
  \]
  The standard Laurent expansion gives a holomorphic extension with \(g(1)\neq0\). After shrinking to a neighborhood \(U\) of \(1\), \(g\) remains nonzero, and on \(U\setminus\{1\}\),
  \[
  -\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}-\frac1{s-1}
  =-\frac{g'(s)}{g(s)}.
  \]
  The right-hand side is holomorphic, hence locally bounded; shrink \(U\) once more to obtain the required bounded-above set of norms.

Finally combine these two independently established statements with conjunction introduction.
